backlink_pages.title: Runbook — Worker Lease Exhaustion
backlink_pages.author: Sam Ortiz
backlink_pages.excerpt: Symptoms Long-running exports hold a lease until the heartbeat expires (NMA-114). Concurrency semaphores leak slots after a panicked handler (NMA-124). Nested null optional fields in job payloads

comments.author: Priya Sharma
comments.body: Load test: 200 forced panics kept inflight_slots oscillating 0–8 instead of climbing to the cap.

content.text: Load test: 200 forced panics kept inflight_slots oscillating 0–8 instead of climbing to the cap.

A handler that panics during Execute leaves the concurrency semaphore permanently acquired. After roughly 64 panics on a worker with max_inflight=64, the process stops accepting new jobs while CPU and memory look idle and the lease renewer is still healthy.

Expected path: recover in the outer run loop releases the slot via defer, then records the panic to the DLQ. Actual path acquires the weighted semaphore before installing the recover defer, so a panic between acquire and defer registration (or inside a non-deferred unlock helper) never returns the weight.

Root cause was acquireSlot() returning a release func that callers were expected to defer, but the panic wrapper called release only on the success and error returns — not on recover. Once max_inflight slots leaked, only a process restart restored throughput.
Hit overnight on the media-thumbnail pool after a nil-pointer regression in an image library upgrade.
